checkpointSupport.description: How well it can be stopped and resumed.

localOnlyEligible.description:
Whether it may run under Local Only.

Computed by the core from the fields above, never taken from the
worker's own claim (`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §7.2).

networkControl.description: What it can do on the network.

unavailableReason.description: Why it is unavailable, when it is.

ApprovalDecisionKind.description: What the user may choose when asked.

oneOf.description: Allow this capability in this project until revoked.

ApprovalDetail.description: One labelled fact shown in an approval prompt.

value.description: The value. Never a secret, never raw file content.

ApprovalId.description: One approval request and its decision.

ApprovalRequest.description: A question put to the user.

approvalId.description: Identifies this question and the decision that answers it.

details.description: Label/value pairs shown beneath the summary. Already redacted.

eligibleDecisions.description:
Which answers are offered.

`AllowProject` is omitted for anything the policy declares
non-persistable, so the interface cannot offer a choice the core would
refuse to honor.

invocationId.description: The invocation waiting on it, when a tool call prompted the question.

riskClass.description: How much damage it could do.

oneOf.description:
Every file change the task's tools reported, in the order they
happened.

ArtifactId.description: Something a task produced and recorded, such as its changed-file summary.

ArtifactProducer.description:
Who produced an artifact.

Records distinguish Tramontana's own facts from claims a worker makes
(`PROJECT_FORMAT.md` §7). Only Tramontana produces artifacts so far.

oneOf.description: Derived by Tramontana from its own records.

ArtifactRecord.description: An artifact recorded against a task.

artifactId.description: Identifies it within the task's record.

byteCount.description: Size of that JSON in bytes.

content.description: The content itself, small enough to carry in the record.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the content's JSON, so a copy can be checked.

label.description: A short, safe name for it.

relation.description: How it relates to the task.

ArtifactRelation.description: How an artifact relates to its task.

oneOf.description: A summary of what the task did.

BundleEntry.description: One file in a bundle, with what a reader needs to trust it.

byteCount.description: Size in bytes, checked against the contents before the checksum.

path.description: Bundle-relative path. Validated on import before it is used.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the contents.

oneOf.description: A budget, deadline, or policy stopped the work.

Capability.description:
What a tool needs permission to do.

A dotted, namespaced name such as `filesystem.read` or `git.read`. Grants
are matched on the exact capability; there is no wildcard and no implied
hierarchy, so `filesystem.read` never confers `filesystem.modify`.

CapabilityScope.description:
What an authorization is limited to.

`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §3.2. A scope binds the project and, for
filesystem work, the canonical roots it may touch. Authorizations are
non-transferable: a grant naming one project authorizes nothing in another.

projectId.description:
The project this is limited to. Absent means a projectless task, which
has no filesystem access at all.

releasesData.description:
Whether the operation sends project-derived data off the device.

A separate dimension from risk: "a read action that sends content to a
cloud endpoint is not treated as a harmless local read"
(`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §3.1).

roots.description: Canonical roots the operation may touch.

CheckpointId.description: A saved checkpoint of a task.

CheckpointSupport.description: How well a worker can be stopped and resumed.

oneOf.description: Can resume itself from its own state.
Can be resumed from canonical Tramontana state by another worker.

CheckpointWorker.description: The worker a checkpoint was taken against.

descriptor.description: Capability facts, snapshotted when the worker was selected.

sessionStateRef.description:
Opaque continuation reference, when the worker offered one.

Adapter data, never the record: a handoff to a different worker ignores
it entirely (`PROJECT_FORMAT.md` §4).

ConfigurationDiagnostic.description:
Something noticed while loading a source.

`CONFIGURATION.md` §5: an invalid or duplicate definition disables the
affected item and shows a validation error. It never crashes startup, and a
broken file in one project must not make the application unusable.

relativePath.description: Project-relative path of the file concerned.

ConfigurationKind.description: What kind of instruction file a source is.

oneOf.description: `AGENTS.md` in a subdirectory, applying to that subtree.
A source kind written by a newer build.

active.description:
Whether this enabled source participates in this resolved manifest.

Nested instructions can be out of scope, while skills, agents, and
workflows must be explicitly selected. Keeping this separate from
`enabled` makes the effective-configuration view honest about both.

byteCount.description:
Size in bytes of the releasable text.

Of the redacted text, for the same reason `content_hash` is: the
number answers "how much of this could be sent", which is what a
context manifest and a release plan are counting.

contentHash.description:
SHA-256 of the source's releasable text, for reproducibility.

Of the *redacted* text, not the bytes on disk. A hash naming content
that may not be released would let a later prompt assembly send the
original and still satisfy every record that describes it
(`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §7). A file with no credential in it
hashes identically either way.

declaredId.description: Declared `id` from front matter, when present.

declaredName.description: Declared `name` from front matter, when present.

enabled.description:
Whether the item is active. Front matter may set `enabled: false`, and
a validation error also disables it.

kind.description: What kind of file it is.

priority.description:
Author-defined rule priority. Higher values apply first within the
native rule layer.

recipes.description:
Commands the project declares. Read from `.tramontana/project.md`
only; declaring one grants nothing (ADR 0025).

redactions.description: Stable codes for credentials removed from this source at ingestion.

relativePath.description: Project-relative path. Never absolute: an absolute path names a machine.

requestedCapabilities.description:
Capabilities requested by a native definition.

These are informational. Loading Markdown never grants a capability.

scopes.description:
Project-relative scopes declared by the source.

A nested `AGENTS.md` contributes its parent directory. Native rules
contribute their `applies_to` patterns. An empty list means the whole
project.

selectionOrder.description: Explicit selection order for skills, agents, and workflows.

sourceId.description: Stable project-scoped key for this source (currently its relative path).

unknownKeys.description:
Front matter keys this build does not recognize.

Preserved rather than dropped, so a file authored for a newer version
survives a round trip through an older one (`CONFIGURATION.md` §5).

ContextCategory.description: Where a piece of context came from.

oneOf.description: The conversation, including the user's goal.
Facts about the repository, such as its branch.

contextManifestId.description: Stable identifier, referenced by routing decisions and checkpoints.

redactions.description: Stable codes for redactions applied before release.

taskId.description: The task this was assembled for.

totalTokenEstimate.description: Approximate total token cost, when estimated.

ContextReleasePlan.description:
Everything one request releases to one destination.

Built by `services::release`, never by hand: the totals and categories are
derived from the payload, so a plan cannot describe a request other than
the one it accompanies.

authorization.description: On whose authority it proceeded. Absent while the plan is a proposal.

contextManifestId.description: The assembled context this payload was drawn from.

dataClasses.description: Data classes actually carried, strongest first.

decisionId.description: The routing decision that chose the destination.

destination.description: The model it is going to.

exclusions.description: Sources assembled for this task that this request did not carry.

messageIds.description: The messages carried, in payload order.

reasonCodes.description: Why the destination was chosen, in the router's deterministic order.

redactions.description: Stable codes for redactions applied before release.

released.description: What was carried, by category and data class.

requiresDisclosure.description:
Whether this release leaves the device.

Derived from `location`, like `RoutingDecision::requires_disclosure`
and for the same reason: whether data left the device is a fact about
where it went, not a judgement a caller should be able to get wrong.

toolsOffered.description:
Tools the model is allowed to call, by name.

Offering a tool to a cloud model discloses that the tool exists and
what it takes, which is part of the release and not an implementation
detail (`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §8).

totalTokenEstimate.description: Approximate total token cost, when one was estimated.

ContextSource.description: One thing that was considered for a context bundle.

byteCount.description: Size of the content in bytes.

category.description: What kind of source it is.

contentHash.description: Hash of the content, so the manifest explains without copying.

exclusionReason.description: Why it was not, when it was not.

redactions.description:
Stable codes for credentials removed from this source at ingestion.

Per source rather than only on the manifest, so a release plan can
report the redactions that apply to what it actually carried instead
of every redaction the task ever made.

sourceId.description: Stable identifier for this source within the task.

tokenEstimate.description: Approximate token cost, when one was estimated.

ConversationId.description: A conversation within a project, or a projectless conversation.

ConversationRecord.description: A conversation, optionally scoped to a project.

archivedAt.description: When it was archived, if it has been.

projectId.description:
Project this belongs to. Absent means projectless, which carries no
implicit filesystem access (`PHASE_1_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md` §8).

CorrelationId.description: A correlation identifier shared by everything caused by one request.

DataClass.description: Sensitivity of a piece of content, used to decide what may leave the device.

oneOf.description: Not derived from the user's project or conversation.
Explicitly marked sensitive by the user or a policy.
A credential or token. Never serialized; see [`SecretRef`].

DestinationClass.description:
Where assembled context is about to go.

The distinction is a policy one, not a technical one: crossing to `Cloud`
is a data-release decision that needs a disclosure, and `Worker` means a
process that is not the model and not Tramontana
(`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §8).

oneOf.description: A model running on this device.

DiagnosticSeverity.description: Why a source was rejected or flagged.

oneOf.description: Loaded, but something is worth knowing.
Not loaded. The item is disabled, and startup continues.

EffectiveConfiguration.description: Everything loaded for a project, in precedence order.

manifestHash.description:
Hash over the ordered source hashes.

One value that changes whenever the effective configuration changes, so
a task can record what it started with in a single field
(`CONFIGURATION.md` §11).

ErrorCode.description:
Stable error categories.

Adapters choose the closest category rather than inventing one; a new
variant is a contract change (`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §15).

oneOf.description: A payload failed validation at a boundary.
The addressed record does not exist.
The operation conflicted with concurrent state, such as a stale sequence.
The operation needs an approval that has not been given.
A standing policy blocked the operation.
The selected model or worker cannot do what was asked.

No credential is stored for the reference that was asked for.

Distinct from [`Self::ProviderAuthentication`], which is a credential
that exists and was refused, and from
[`Self::ProviderUnavailable`], which is a credential store that could
not be reached. Collapsing the three would make "you need to sign in
again" the answer to a locked Keychain
(`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §7).
The provider applied a rate limit.
The provider is unreachable or unhealthy.
The selected worker is unreachable or unhealthy.
A size, count, depth, or budget limit was exceeded.
A protocol peer sent something malformed.
Stored data needs a migration that has not run.
Work stopped with an action whose replay safety is unknown.

correlationId.description: Correlates this failure with the request and events around it.

diagnosticRef.description: Reference to fuller local diagnostics, which are redacted separately.

message.description: Safe, user-presentable message. Never carries secrets or content.

retryAfterMs.description: Hint for how long to wait before retrying, when the source supplies one.

retryable.description: Whether retrying the identical request could succeed.

causationId.description: The command, event, invocation, or approval that caused this one.

conversationId.description: Conversation, when the task has one.

correlationId.description: Shared by everything caused by one originating request.

kind.description:
The event kind, duplicated outside the payload so a reader can route on
it without parsing a body it may not understand.

sequence.description: Position in the task's stream. Starts at 1, increases by exactly one.

EventPayload.description:
The body of a durable event.

Tagged by `kind` so the discriminator is one field in both Rust and
TypeScript. M1 defines the payloads the walking skeleton emits; the rest
arrive with the milestones that produce them.

oneOf.description: A bounded explanation of a core lifecycle decision.

conversationId.description: Conversation this task belongs to, when it has one.

goalSummary.description: One-line, secret-free summary of what was asked for.

routingMode.description:
Where this task's models may run, chosen when it was created and
kept if it is resumed.

Absent from tasks recorded before the mode was, which resume under
the profile's mode (ADR 0031).

oneOf.description: Effective configuration was resolved before execution began.

configuration.description: Secret-free manifest metadata. Markdown bodies are not copied.

oneOf.description:
A context bundle was assembled for a destination.

Carries the manifest whole rather than an identifier, because the
record has to explain a data release without a second lookup — and
because an exported bundle must still explain it on a machine that has
none of the original storage.

manifest.description: What was assembled, and what was withheld.

oneOf.description:
A payload was released to a destination, on a recorded authority.

Separate from `contextPrepared` because assembling is not sending. One
assembly can produce several releases — a fallback that crosses to a
different destination is a second one — and each has its own
disclosure and its own approval (`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §8).

plan.description:
What went, where, and on whose authority.

Boxed because it is by far the largest payload, and every event in
the system is moved by value: without the indirection each of the
twenty-odd other variants would carry its footprint.

oneOf.description: A model and a location were chosen.

decision.description: The decision, its reasons, and the context it released.

oneOf.description:
A worker was selected for this task.

Carries the whole descriptor rather than a name, because a checkpoint
is derived from this stream and a handoff needs the capability facts
(`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §5.1, `PROJECT_FORMAT.md` §4). Recording only an
identifier would mean a resumed task had to ask a provider what it once
was, which is exactly the dependency a portable record must not have.

streamId.description: Correlates the ephemeral stream frames with this durable event.

oneOf.description: A durable normalized message was committed.

A worker asked to run a tool.

Carries a *summary* of the arguments, never the arguments themselves:
they can hold file content or other project data, and the durable
stream is displayed and exported (`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §5).

argumentsSummary.description: Short, safe description of what was asked for.

invocationId.description: Identifies this invocation across its request and result.

requestHash.description: Hash of the tool identity and normalized arguments, never raw values.

riskClass.description: How much damage the tool could do.

stepId.description: Worker-supplied stable step identity, scoped to this task.

oneOf.description:
A permission decision was reached.

Emitted for *every* decision, including the ones nobody was asked
about. The exit criterion for M3 is that every action carries an
origin, a scope, and a decision — a silently-permitted action would
satisfy the permission system and fail the audit requirement.

grantKind.description: How the authorization was obtained, when it was allowed.

replaySafety.description: Effect classification recorded before execution. Legacy events are unknown.

changes.description:
The files this invocation changed, as the tool reported them.
Absent from records written before tools reported changes
(ADR 0026).

displaySummary.description: Short, safe description of the result.

truncated.description: Whether output was cut short by a limit.

oneOf.description: Something the task produced, recorded as Tramontana's own fact.

A checkpoint was written.

The checkpoint itself lives in its own repository; this event records
that one exists at this point in the stream, and enough of it to be
read without a second lookup.

completedStepCount.description: How many steps it records as already done.

eventSequence.description: The durable sequence it was taken at.

pendingAction.description: What was in flight, when anything was.

resume.description: Whether the task can be picked up again from here.

artifacts.description: Artifacts the task recorded, such as the files it changed.

origin.description: Who or what asked for cancellation.

oneOf.description:
An event kind this build does not understand.

Reading one is not an error: a newer core may write kinds an older
interface has never heard of, and the contract requires storing and
displaying them rather than failing (`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §2).

ExecutionLocation.description:
Where work ran.

Recorded on routing decisions and shown to the user, so "did this leave my
machine?" is answerable from the durable record alone.

targetId.description: Stable identifier for the compute target.

oneOf.description: A third-party endpoint. Reaching one is a data-release decision.

region.description: Provider region, when the provider exposes one.

bundleMajorVersion.description: Major version of the bundle layout. Refused when unrecognized.

bundleMinorVersion.description: Minor version. A reader may ignore what it does not know.

omissions.description: What was left out, and how much.

options.description: What the export chose to include.

projectId.description: The project, when the export was scoped to one.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the records inside the bundle.

ExportOptions.description:
What an export chose to include.

Absent means the default, which is to exclude. The flags exist so a bundle
records the decision that produced it rather than leaving a reader to infer
it from what happens to be present.

includeAbsolutePaths.description: Keep absolute device paths instead of redacting them.

ExportedConfiguration.description:
A configuration manifest with the project it belongs to.

The manifest itself does not name its project — it is stored under one —
so a bundle has to carry the pairing. Without it an imported task would
reference a manifest nothing could resolve, and the record could not say
which instructions were in force when the work happened.

configuration.description: The secret-free manifest. Instruction bodies are not copied.

projectId.description: The project this manifest was resolved for.

FileChange.description: What one invocation did to one file, as the tool that did it reports.

alreadyApplied.description:
Whether the tool found the change already made and changed nothing
now: a replay after an interruption, or content that was already
there.

contentHash.description:
Hash of the content afterwards; for a deletion, of the content that
was removed and kept for recovery.

from.description: For a move, the project-relative path it had before.

path.description:
The project-relative path the file has now; for a deletion, the path
it had.

previousHash.description: For an edit, the hash of the content before it.

FileChangeKind.description: The kinds of change a file tool makes.

oneOf.description: A file got a new name.
No approval was needed: a read inside an already-opened project.
Approved for exactly this request, and consumed by it.
A persistent, revocable grant for this project and capability.

HandoffBundle.description:
Everything a different worker needs to continue a task.

Assembled from canonical records only. A worker's opaque continuation data
is never read to build this, which is what makes the claim in
`PROJECT_FORMAT.md` §4 — that canonical state is sufficient — testable
rather than aspirational.

completedStepIds.description: Steps already done, which the receiving worker must not repeat.

configurationManifestHash.description: The effective configuration in force, for a project task.

conversationId.description: Its conversation, when it has one.

omissions.description: What this handoff does not carry.

pendingAction.description: What was in flight, when anything was.

previousWorker.description:
The worker that had the task, for provenance only.

A receiving worker is told who held it before, not asked to imitate
them. Nothing private to that worker is carried.

projectId.description: Its project, when it has one.

HandoffEntry.description: One fact in a handoff, normalized so any worker can read it.

kind.description: What kind of fact this is.

sequence.description: Position in the task's durable stream.

Health.description: Whether a provider or worker is usable right now.

oneOf.description: A separate process speaking the Agent Client Protocol.
A separate process speaking something bespoke.

MessageId.description: A durable message in a conversation.

oneOf.description: A request to run a tool.

arguments.description: Arguments, already validated against the tool's schema.

oneOf.description: The result of running a tool.

truncated.description: Whether output was cut short by a limit.

oneOf.description: A part this build does not understand.
A tool result being fed back.
Stream ended early; content up to that point was kept.
Replaced by a later message, retained for history.

ModelControl.description: Who decides which model a worker uses.

oneOf.description: Every model request passes through Tramontana's router and policy.
The worker calls models itself. Not equivalent to brokered.

contextLimit.description: Context window, when the provider reports one.

healthReasonCode.description: Stable reason for a non-available health, for diagnostics and tests.

location.description: Whether inference runs on this device or elsewhere.

ModelEvent.description:
One item from a model stream.

Exactly one [`ModelEvent::Completed`] or [`ModelEvent::Failed`] ends a
stream, even when cancellation arrives while the underlying request is
still in flight (`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §8). The shared provider contract
suite checks that for every adapter.

offset.description: Zero-based ordinal shared by text/tool deltas (not a byte offset).

oneOf.description: Incremental arguments for a tool call the model is assembling.

callId.description: Provider call identifier, supplied on the opening fragment.

callIndex.description:
Stable position of this call within the response. Continuations
carry the same index even when the provider omits its identifier.

name.description: Tool name, supplied on the opening fragment. Never inferred from ID.

offset.description: Zero-based ordinal shared by text/tool deltas (not a byte offset).

ModelLimits.description:
Bounds on one request.

`deadlineMs` is required rather than optional: a request with no deadline
is one that can hang a task forever, and every provider has to honour the
same bound for cancellation to mean the same thing everywhere.

deadlineMs.description: How long the whole request may take.

maxOutputTokens.description: Cap on generated tokens, when one applies.

ModelLocation.description: Whether a model runs on this device.

oneOf.description: A third-party endpoint. Reaching one is a data-release decision.

contextManifestId.description: The context release this request was built from.

dataClasses.description: How sensitive the content is, for routing and disclosure.

messages.description: The conversation so far, already normalized and redacted.

requestId.description: Correlates this request with its `modelStarted` event and its stream.

requiredCapabilities.description:
Capabilities a model must have to serve this request.

The router matches these; a provider that cannot meet them is not a
fallback, it is ineligible.

responseFormat.description: What shape of answer was asked for.

taskId.description: The task on whose behalf it is made.

tools.description: Tools the model may call, as the model sees them.

NetworkControl.description: What a worker can do on the network.

oneOf.description: Egress is limited by a tested boundary.
Egress cannot be observed. Disqualifying for Local Only.

conversationId.description:
Conversation this message belongs to, when it has one.

Optional because a task can be started outside a conversation, and its
assistant answer is still the durable record of what the model said.
Dropping the message because there was no conversation would leave the
exported task with tool calls and no answer.

taskId.description: Task that produced it, when one did.

NormalizedToolDefinition.description:
A tool as a model is told about it.

Deliberately not [`ToolDescriptor`](super::ToolDescriptor): that type
carries the risk class, capability, and cancellation facts Tramontana uses
to *govern* a call. A model needs the name, the purpose, and the argument
shape, and nothing else.

description.description: What it does, in the words the model sees.

name.description: Namespaced tool identifier, as the model should call it.

Omission.description: One thing an export left out, and how much of it.

reason.description: Why it was left out, in a sentence a person can act on.

OmissionCategory.description: What kind of data was left out of an export.

oneOf.description: A secret reference or credential-store value. Never included.
An absolute device path, which names a machine and often a person.
An internal audit marker never shown outside the application.

PendingAction.description: The one action that had started and not finished.

displaySummary.description: Short, secret-free description for a person deciding what to do.

kind.description: What kind of action it was.

referenceId.description: The invocation, request, or approval it refers to.

PendingActionKind.description: What kind of work was in flight when the task stopped.

oneOf.description: A model request had started and not returned.
A tool invocation had started and not reported an outcome.
A question had been put to the user and not answered.
A worker session had started and not stopped.

PermissionOrigin.description:
Who asked for a capability.

An audit record that cannot say *who* asked is not an audit record. A
built-in tool invoked by the user and the same tool invoked by an external
worker are different events, even when the arguments match.

oneOf.description: A worker acting on the task.

grantId.description: Stable identifier, so it can be shown and revoked.

riskCeiling.description: The highest risk it covers. A grant never escalates.

ProjectId.description: A project: one or more user-approved roots and the work done against them.

ProjectRecord.description: A project and the roots the user approved for it.

roots.description: Canonical approved roots. Device-local bindings, redacted on export.

Recipe.description:
A command a project declares for a person to approve running, such as its
test suite.

An argument list with the program first, never a command line: no shell
ever sees it. Each run is its own approval, showing exactly this list
(ADR 0025).

id.description: Stable id, unique within the project.

ReleaseAuthorization.description: On whose authority a release proceeded.

approvalId.description: The approval that permitted it, when a user was asked.

mode.description: The routing mode in force, which is the standing policy that applied.

ReleaseExclusion.description: A source that was assembled and did not go.

category.description: What kind of source it is.

reasonCode.description: Stable reason it did not go.

ReleasedCategory.description:
One category of content actually carried by a request.

Summarized by category and data class rather than listed source by source:
the disclosure has to be readable before a person decides, and
`PHASE_1_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md` §12 asks for categories, classes, and a
size estimate — not a file listing.

byteCount.description: How many bytes of them were carried.

category.description: What kind of source it is.

sourceCount.description: How many sources of this kind were carried.

ReplaySafety.description:
Whether repeating an action is safe.

This is a statement about *effects*, not about whether the action would
succeed. Reading a file twice is safe; writing one twice may not be, and a
tool whose effects are not known is treated as though they are not.

oneOf.description: Repeating it changes nothing outside Tramontana.
Repeating it could duplicate an effect.
Not determinable from the record. Treated as [`ReplaySafety::Unsafe`].

ResponseFormat.description: What shape of answer was asked for.

schema.description: The schema the answer must satisfy.

ResumeEligibility.description: Whether, and how, this checkpoint can be resumed.

eligible.description: Whether resuming is offered at all.

reasonCode.description: Stable reason, present whenever the answer needs explaining.

ResumeMode.description: How a task may be picked up again.

oneOf.description: The worker that was running it continues.
A different worker continues from canonical Tramontana state.

RiskClass.description: How much damage a tool invocation could do if the model asked for it wrongly.

oneOf.description: Hard to reverse, broad, privileged, external, or destructive.

RoutedModel.description: One model a decision could use.

RoutingDecision.description: Where a task's inference was sent, and why.

availabilitySnapshotId.description:
The availability snapshot the decision was made against.

Recorded so a decision can be explained later even though availability
has moved on. Without it, "why not the other model?" is unanswerable.

fallbackOrder.description: What would have been tried next, in order.

mode.description: The routing mode in force when it was made.

requiresDisclosure.description: Whether reaching this route needs the user told.

RoutingFallback.description: A model and where it would run, as a fallback option.

RoutingMode.description: The user's standing policy for where inference may run.

oneOf.description: Hard egress prohibition for inference and cloud-derived context.
Deterministic policy chooses an eligible route and shows its reasons.
Prefer a configured cloud route where policy and availability allow.

SecretRef.description:
An opaque handle to a credential.

This is the only representation of a secret that may be persisted, logged,
exported, or sent over IPC. `key` is an application-generated identifier
and never carries any part of the value it refers to
(`SECURITY_AND_PERMISSIONS.md` §7).

key.description: Opaque application-generated key. Never the secret.

SecretStore.description:
Where a resolvable secret lives.

Only `Platform` exists today. It is an enum rather than a bare marker so
that adding a store later is an additive schema change.

SideEffect.description: What an invocation actually changed, recorded alongside its result.

oneOf.description: Nothing outside Tramontana's own records changed.
A local change that can be undone.
A local change that cannot be undone.
The model asked to call a tool.

StreamFrame.description:
One frame of an in-flight model stream.

Explicitly **not** an [`EventEnvelope`]: frames are transport, are never
persisted, and carry no sequence in the durable stream. A reconnecting
interface rebuilds from durable events plus, optionally, the current
stream snapshot.

offset.description: Monotonically increasing position within this stream.

streamId.description: Correlates with the `modelStarted` event that opened this stream.

TaskCheckpoint.description:
A point a task can be understood from and continued at.

Two fields deviate from the shape written in `CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §11, and
the document has been updated to match: `worker`, `contextManifestId`, and
`configurationManifestHash` are optional here. A task interrupted while
`preparing` has not selected a worker or prepared a context, and a
projectless task never has a configuration manifest
(`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §5.2). Requiring them would mean either inventing
values or refusing to checkpoint exactly the tasks a checkpoint is most
needed for.

completedStepIds.description:
Steps already done, which resume must not repeat.

The watermark, not a log: a step named here has a durable completion
event behind it.

configurationManifestHash.description: The effective configuration in force, for a project task.

contextManifestId.description: The context bundle prepared for this task, when one was.

eventSequence.description:
The durable sequence this checkpoint was taken at.

Everything at or below this sequence is accounted for by the fields
here; anything above it happened afterwards.

pendingAction.description: The action that had started and not finished, when there was one.

resume.description: Whether and how this can be picked up again.

taskState.description: The task's state at that sequence.

worker.description: The worker, when one had been selected.

TaskEventKind.description:
What a durable event is about.

`#[non_exhaustive]` and the `Unsupported` fallback in
[`EventPayload`] together implement the compatibility rule in
`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §2: an unknown event kind is stored and shown as an
unsupported redacted event, never a crash.

oneOf.description: A model and location were chosen.
A payload was released to a destination.
A durable normalized message was committed.
A worker asked to run a tool.
An approval was put to the user.
A bounded, redacted diagnostic was recorded.

TaskId.description: A unit of work with its own event stream and exactly one terminal state.

TaskRecord.description:
A task row.

`state` and `last_sequence` are a cache of the event stream, not a second
source of truth. After an unclean stop they are rebuilt from the events.

configurationManifestHash.description: Effective-configuration manifest captured before this task started.

conversationId.description: Conversation this belongs to, when it has one.

goalSummary.description: Secret-free summary of what was asked for.

projectId.description: Project this belongs to, when it has one.

state.description: Cached state, projected from the events.

updatedAt.description: When the projection was last updated.

TaskSnapshot.description:
The current view of a task.

A projection of the event stream, not a second source of truth: it exists
so reading a task's state does not require replaying every event.

TaskState.description: Where a task is in its lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Choosing a model and a compute target.
The worker is doing the work. Model and tool activity are events here.
Stopped uncleanly. Not automatically resumable — a checkpoint decides.

TaskUpdate.description:
One item delivered to a task subscriber.

Durable events and ephemeral frames share a channel so a subscriber sees
them interleaved in the order they happened, but they stay distinct
variants: only [`TaskUpdate::Event`] carries a sequence, and only it
survives a restart. An interface that treats a frame as durable will lose
it on reconnect and be surprised; the type makes that hard to do by
accident.

oneOf.description:
A durable event.

Boxed because an envelope is far larger than a frame, and frames are
the high-frequency variant: without the indirection every frame on the
channel would carry the envelope's footprint. The serialized shape is
unaffected.
An ephemeral model stream frame. Never persisted.

Timestamp.description: An instant, serialized as a UTC RFC 3339 string.

oneOf.description: Every effect is requested through the host and passes policy.
Direct access, confined by a tested compute boundary.
Direct access with no confinement. Cannot meet the Phase 1 contract.

ToolDescriptor.description: A tool the registry can offer to a worker.

description.description: What it does, for the approval prompt. Presentation, never policy.

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema its arguments are validated against.

replaySafety.description:
What re-invoking the same step, with the same arguments, would do.

Declared by the tool rather than inferred from [`Self::side_effect`]. A
tool that writes can still be safe to replay if it verifies the world
before acting — creating a file only if it is absent, and reporting an
identical existing file as already applied — and a tool with no side
effect may still decline the claim.

Recovery trusts this value: a step declared `safe` is re-invoked on
resume, and anything else leaves the task for a person to reconcile.
An over-claim therefore breaks the resume promise silently
(`BUILD_ORDER.md` §16), which is why every tool declaring `safe` with a
side effect must pass `testing::contract_suites::idempotent_tool_contract`.

Absent means `unknown`, never `safe`.

riskClass.description: How much damage it could do.

estimated.description:
Whether these are counted or approximated.

Recorded rather than hidden: a cost shown to a user as exact when it was
estimated is a number they will make decisions on.

Visibility.description:
Who an event is for.

Redaction happens in core before delivery, so `Secret` events are internal
audit markers holding references and hashes only, and never reach a webview
(`CORE_CONTRACTS.md` §5).

oneOf.description: Shown in the normal activity stream.
Available in diagnostics, not in the primary stream.
Internal audit marker; never delivered to the user interface.
